items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of education and professional experience.

Advanced degree in communications, public affairs, journalism, marketing, business, or a related discipline; OR graduate degree in an energy or transportation related field of study, such as engineering, environmental science or policy, etc.
Extensive progressively responsible experience managing comprehensive communications programs in higher education, research, government, nonprofit, or similarly complex organizations.
Experience supporting research organizations, academic institutions, or federally funded research programs.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing strategic communications plans across multiple communications disciplines.
Experience supporting executive leadership, fundraising initiatives, and strategic partnerships.
Experience supervising professional communications staff and managing multidisciplinary communications projects.
Experience managing media relations, digital communications, publications, branding, and stakeholder engagement.

Under general direction of the Chief Administrative Officer and reporting to the Director of the Institute of Transportation Studies and the Executive Director of the Energy & Efficiency Institute, strategically plan, manage, and independently oversee a comprehensive, multidisciplinary communications program supporting the Transportation and Energy Research Cluster, including the Institutes’ affiliated research centers, initiatives, and academic programs. Develop and implement integrated communications strategies that advance institutional priorities, elevate the visibility and impact of research, strengthen stakeholder engagement, support fundraising and partnership development, increase student enrollment and engagement, and enhance the reputation of the Cluster at the regional, national, and international levels.
35% - Strategic Communications Leadership

Serve as the principal communications advisor to institute leadership, faculty directors, and senior administrators on strategic communications planning, messaging, branding, media relations, issues management, executive communications, and public engagement. Manage a comprehensive communications program spanning multiple communications disciplines, including strategic communications, marketing, digital communications, publications, media relations, social media, web communications, multimedia production, events, and visual communications.
25% - Integrated Communications, Marketing, and Digital Strategy

As a member of the Cluster’s leadership team, establish communications priorities, develop long- and short-term strategic communications plans, allocate communications resources, and evaluate program effectiveness through measurable outcomes. Ensure communications activities align with university priorities, identity standards, and organizational objectives while effectively translating complex scientific and technical research into compelling communications for policymakers, government agencies, industry leaders, sponsors, faculty, students, media, and the public.
20% - External Relations, Partnerships, and Organizational Engagement

Manage professional staff, student employees, and contracted communications professionals while fostering a collaborative, innovative, and service-oriented communications organization that delivers high-quality products within established timelines and available resources.
20% - Program Administration and Personnel Management

Demonstrated ability to communicate complex scientific, technical, or policy information for diverse audiences.
Knowledge of transportation, energy, sustainability, climate, engineering, or public policy issues.
Strong analytical, organizational, project management, and budget management skills.
